Stack, integrations & measures

Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

Industry systems

What we integrate with.

Examples of systems commonly found in financial services. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

Loan origination and management (LOS and LMS)

Hold applications, sanctions, repayment schedules and loan accounts. Trackers, reminders and top-up lists read from here, and credit decisions stay in the LOS, recorded by credit staff.

  • Nucleus FinnOne Neo
  • Lentra
  • Salesforce Financial Services Cloud
  • In-house LOS and LMS

KYC, consent and verification rails

Used by the regulated entity to verify identity, fetch documents and bank data with consent, and capture signatures. We connect through the entity's own contracts and integrations, never around them.

  • CKYC Registry (CERSAI)
  • DigiLocker
  • Video KYC platforms (for example IDfy or HyperVerge)
  • Account Aggregator network
  • eSign (for example Leegality or Digio)

Credit bureaus, mandates and payment gateways

Bureau checks are run by the credit team. Mandate results and gateways supply repayment status and hosted payment links for reminders and collections.

  • TransUnion CIBIL
  • Experian
  • CRIF High Mark
  • NACH via sponsor bank and UPI AutoPay
  • Razorpay, Cashfree or PayU

Insurance distribution systems

Hold proposals, policies, renewals and claims. Renewal reminders and claim trackers read from these systems, and underwriting and claim decisions remain with insurers and TPAs.

  • Broker or agency management system
  • Insurer partner portals and APIs
  • TPA portals
  • POSP quoting platforms
  • Bima Bharosa grievance portal

Mutual fund platforms, RTAs and KRAs

Supply holdings, transactions, SIP status and KYC status for onboarding and reviews. Transactions are placed by the adviser, distributor or client through these platforms, not by the automation.

  • BSE StAR MF
  • NSE NMF II
  • CAMS and KFintech
  • MF Central
  • CVL KRA
  • Investwell or REDVision back office

Payments, disputes and risk operations

Generate disputes and alerts and hold the evidence. Queues and summaries read from here, and analysts submit responses and take actions in the source systems.

  • Payment gateway or PA console
  • Visa Resolve Online and Mastercom
  • NPCI UDIR
  • Transaction monitoring or risk engine
  • I4C CFCFRMS

CRM, service desk, dialers and data

Own the customer record, tickets and call logs. Consent flags, contact rules and outcomes are written back here so reporting reconciles across teams.

  • Salesforce, Zoho CRM or HubSpot
  • Freshdesk or Zendesk
  • Dialer with 1600-series numbers
  • Google BigQuery or Snowflake

Key measures

The KPIs we propose to track.

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

First response time to inquiries

Median elapsed time from a new inquiry on any connected channel to the first meaningful reply by the system or a person, by channel, product and hour of day.

Why it matters: Borrowers, buyers and investors contact several providers at once, and a fast, honest first reply often earns the application.

Files complete at first submission

Applications, proposals or merchant files with every required document and KYC step complete when first sent for decision, divided by all files sent for decision in the period.

Why it matters: Incomplete files are the main source of rework and delay for credit, underwriting and onboarding teams.

Application turnaround time

Median elapsed time from a complete application to a recorded decision, and from decision to disbursal, issuance or activation, by product and channel.

Why it matters: Turnaround shapes conversion as much as price, and splitting it by stage shows where files wait.

Onboarding drop-off by step

Share of applicants who start but do not finish each onboarding step, such as document upload, Video KYC, bank verification or mandate setup, by channel and cohort.

Why it matters: Drop-off concentrates in a few steps, and fixing those steps recovers applicants who already chose you.

Mandate bounce and cure rate

EMI or SIP debits that fail on presentation, divided by all debits presented, and the share of bounced debits paid within the agreed cure window, by product, bank and reason code.

Why it matters: Early, respectful follow-up after a bounce keeps accounts current and reduces later collections effort.

Renewals before expiry

Policies renewed on or before their expiry date, divided by policies due in the period, by line of business, insurer and channel.

Why it matters: Lapsed policies leave customers uninsured, lose continuity benefits and often move to another distributor.

Claims beyond regulatory timeline

Claims supported by the broker or agency that remain open past the applicable IRDAI settlement timeline, counted and aged by insurer and claim type.

Why it matters: Shows where escalation with the insurer is needed before the customer has to complain.

Disputes answered within deadline

Chargebacks and payment disputes responded to before the network or regulatory deadline, divided by all disputes received in the period.

Why it matters: A missed deadline is usually an automatic loss, regardless of the evidence available.

Alert time to first analyst action

Median time from a fraud or risk alert being raised to an analyst's first recorded action, by severity band.

Why it matters: In account takeover and mule cases, minutes decide whether funds can still be held.

Grievances resolved within timeline

Complaints closed within the internal service timeline, divided by complaints received, by category, with the age of open complaints tracked daily.

Why it matters: A borrower who gets no reply within thirty days can approach the RBI Ombudsman, and insurance and securities complaints have their own escalation routes.

Integration principles

How we connect systems responsibly.

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
